match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the economic and social impacts of trade on Australia, such as cheaper imports, factory closures, job shifts to services and population change: 'Changing trade links' covers shifting partners, 'Trade links places' covers the basic definition of trade, and 'Impacts of tourism' covers a different industry.

draft.title: Impacts of trade on Australia
card: Trade has given Australian shoppers cheaper goods. Many clothes, appliances and electronics are now imported from countries where they cost less to make.
Cheaper imports made it hard for some local factories to compete. Many closed. Car making in Australia is one example: the last big car factories shut in 2017.
Jobs have moved towards services, such as health, education, retail and tourism. Some workers who lost factory jobs had to retrain or move to find new work.
Towns that relied on one factory can be changed a great deal. Some lose people and shops as workers leave, while larger cities with many services have tended to grow.
draft.remember: Imports made goods cheaper, but factory closures shifted jobs to services and changed some towns.

a.q: Which change is a result of cheaper imports for Australia?
opts: Many local factories closed as they could not compete
Australia stopped buying goods from other countries
Wages in all Australian industries rose quickly
Services jobs became less common in Australian cities
a.why: Cheaper imported goods made it hard for local factories to compete on price, so many closed. Services jobs grew, not shrank, and Australia still imports many goods.
a.clue: Think about what happens to a local maker when a cheaper product arrives from overseas.

b.q: A town in Victoria had one large factory making appliances. It closed after cheaper imported appliances took its customers. Which outcome is most likely for the town?
opts: Some workers leave to find jobs, so its population may fall
Its population grows as shoppers pay less for appliances
Every worker is quickly hired by a new local factory
The town gains no benefit from cheaper imports at all
b.why: When a main employer closes, workers may leave to find work elsewhere, so the population may fall. The town's shoppers still gain from cheaper goods, but that does not stop the loss of jobs.
b.clue: Where do workers go when the only big local employer shuts?

a.best: Many local factories closed as they could not compete

b.best: Some workers leave to find jobs, so its population may fall

problems.detail: The right option is the only hedged one ('some', 'may'), while two distractors use absolutes ('Every worker', 'no benefit ... at all'). A student could pick it by spotting the qualifier without knowing the idea.
